answer.rationale: Primary region write path latency is 5x target and climbing, confined to primary region. The release carries a mandatory security patch that cannot be reverted, eliminating rollback. Regional failover (memory_b2) successfully restored latency during prior degradation with clean traffic shift and fast error rate recovery. With settlement traffic at daily peak, redirecting writes to a healthy secondary region will shed load from the degraded primary while preserving the security patch. Read-replica routing addresses reporting load, not write latency. Circuit breakers mitigate cascading failures but don't address the root cause. Capacity addition would be slower than failover. Memory_b2 validates that failover works cleanly in this infrastructure during latency events.
